mainTopic: Resisting sin, reward and punishment for deeds and thoughts, and the severity of חילול השם
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story about a sage who came through a dangerous night safely. The רבנן explain that whoever escapes a sin of ערוה gets a miracle, and they tell how רבי צדוק sat in a burning oven and רב כהנא jumped from a roof rather than sin. Then רבא challenges רב נחמן: the משנה in פאה lists only a few מצוות that pay 'fruits' in this world, so why is שילוח הקן missing? The answer is that the list holds only מצוות that are good to people as well as to Heaven. The גמרא teaches that a זכות earns principal and fruits, while an עבירה earns fruits only if it causes further results. A good thought is credited as a deed. A bad thought is not, unless it leads to action or involves עבודה זרה. The amud ends with teachings on how severe public חילול השם is: sinning privately is less bad, אין מקיפין בחילול השם, and a new ברייתא begins with 'Always', continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: The sage says royal guards protected him all night
steps.stepSummary: The sage (רבי חנינא בר פפי) tells the רבנן that soldiers of the king guarded him all night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The king's guards watched over me the whole night.
steps.whatsHappening: We are picking up at the end of a story. The sage had hidden in a dangerous place to run away from sin, and the רבנן asked him who protected him. Here he answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He says royal soldiers kept him safe through the night. The רבנן hear that he came through unharmed, and in the next step they suggest the real reason was a miracle earned by holding back from sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Soldiers of the king (literally 'bearers of Caesar')

phrases.english: Soldiers of the king
phrases.notes: Literally 'bearers of Caesar,' meaning the king's armed guards.

phrases.english: guarded me all night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a story that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sage says royal soldiers guarded him all night.

steps.title: Escaping a sin of ערוה brings a miracle
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן suggest he got a miracle because he avoided a sin of ערוה, and they back this up with a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Maybe a chance to sin with a forbidden woman came your way and you held back, because we learned that anyone who holds back from such a sin gets a miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן explain why the miracle happened. They quote a teaching that whoever escapes a sin of ערוה has a miracle done for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The miracle in the story is not random. It is a reward for holding back. The ברייתא turns one story into a general rule.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Perhaps a matter of forbidden relations came your way
and you were saved from it,
as we learned:
Anyone to whom a matter of forbidden relations comes
and he is saved from it,
a miracle is done for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the miracle from Step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the sage's miracle came because he escaped a sin.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: anyone who escapes a sin of ערוה has a miracle done for him.

steps.title: The פסוק about the 'mighty in strength' points to רבי צדוק
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in תהלים is read as describing people like רבי צדוק and his colleagues, who overcame temptation.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Mighty in strength who do His word, listening to the voice of His word.' This means people like רבי צדוק and his colleagues.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching continues with a פסוק and names the kind of people it describes. This line sets up the stories that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real 'strength' here means beating your own desires, not physical power. Naming רבי צדוק leads straight into his story, and רב כהנא's story then shows the same kind of strength.

phrases.english: "Mighty in strength who do His word,
phrases.notes: תהלים 103:20

phrases.english: hearkening to the voice of His word" —
such as Rabbi Tzadok and his colleagues.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a פסוק to the ברייתא and names examples.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'mighty in strength' are people like רבי צדוק who overcome temptation.

steps.title: רבי צדוק stalls by asking for food
steps.stepSummary: A noblewoman tries to seduce רבי צדוק. He says he is weak and asks for food, and she offers non-kosher food. He answers that someone who does this sin may as well eat that food.
steps.simpleTranslation: A noblewoman tried to seduce רבי צדוק. He said: My heart is weak and I can't. Is there something to eat? She said: There is non-kosher food. He said: What difference does it make? Whoever does this also eats this.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first part of רבי צדוק's story. He is buying time, and the scene is being set for what he does next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words 'one who does this eats this' sound like he is giving in. Really he is stalling. The non-kosher food on the fire sets up the oven in the next step.

phrases.english: A certain noblewoman tried to seduce Rabbi Tzadok.
He said to her: My heart is weak
and I am not able;
is there something to eat?
She said to him: There is something non-kosher.
He said to her: What difference does it make?
One who does this, eats this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the story of רבי צדוק, who was named in Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי צדוק stalls when he is tempted to sin.

steps.title: רבי צדוק sits in the burning oven
steps.stepSummary: While she cooks the food, רבי צדוק climbs into the hot oven, explaining that whoever does this sin falls into this fire. She backs off.
steps.simpleTranslation: She lit the oven and put the food in. He climbed up and sat inside it. She said: What is this? He said: Whoever does that sin falls into this fire. She said: Had I known it meant so much to you, I would not have pained you.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the climax of the story. רבי צדוק would rather sit in fire than sin, and the woman gives up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He changes his earlier words: before, it was 'does this, eats this'; now it is 'does this, falls into this.' He shows her that the sin leads to burning punishment, so a real fire is better. This is the miracle-worthy self-control the ברייתא described.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי צדוק was willing to suffer real physical harm rather than sin. That is the 'strength' of the פסוק, and רב כהנא's story in the next steps shows the same thing.

phrases.english: She lit the oven,
and was placing it (the food) in it.
He climbed up and sat inside it.
She said to him: What is this?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: דְּעָבֵיד הָא – נָפֵיל בְּהָא.
phrases.english: He said to her: One who does this, falls into this.
phrases.notes: He is hinting at the fire of punishment that waits for a person who does this sin.

phrases.aramaic: אַמְרַהּ לֵיהּ: אִי יָדְעִי כּוּלֵּי הַאי –
phrases.english: She said to him: Had I known it was all this,
I would not have caused you pain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי צדוק's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי צדוק risks being burned rather than sin, and is saved.

steps.title: רב כהנא jumps off the roof and אליהו catches him
steps.stepSummary: A noblewoman tries to seduce רב כהנא, who sold baskets. He says he will go get ready, then throws himself off the roof. אליהו catches him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא was selling baskets, and a noblewoman tried to seduce him. He said: Let me go fix myself up. He went up and threw himself from the roof toward the ground. אליהו came and caught him.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story with the same lesson. רב כהנא risks his life to avoid sin, and a miracle saves him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the rule from Step 2 in action: he escaped a sin of ערוה, and a miracle was done for him (אליהו catching him).

phrases.english: Rav Kahana was selling baskets;
a certain noblewoman tried to seduce him.
He said to her: Let me go and adorn myself.
He went up and was falling from the roof to the ground.
Elijah came and caught him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second example of the rule from Step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב כהנא escapes sin and is saved by a miracle.

steps.title: Poverty caused the danger, so אליהו gives him money
steps.stepSummary: אליהו complains that he had to travel 400 פרסאות. רב כהנא answers that poverty put him in this spot, and אליהו gives him a basket of דינרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו said: You made me travel 400 פרסאות! רב כהנא said: What caused this? Wasn't it poverty? אליהו gave him a basket of דינרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רב כהנא explains that he was only in this situation because he was poor, and אליהו fixes the root problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being poor forced רב כהנא into a job that kept putting him in the path of temptation. אליהו does more than save him once: he removes the cause, so it won't happen again.
steps.whatToRemember: Holding back from sin brings a miracle. A wise person also removes what keeps leading him toward the sin.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַטְרַחְתַּן אַרְבַּע מְאָה פַּרְסֵי!
phrases.english: He said to him: You troubled me four hundred parasangs!
He said to him: What caused me this,
was it not poverty?
He gave him a basket of dinars.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב כהנא's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אליהו removes רב כהנא's poverty, which had led him into temptation.

steps.title: רבא begins a contradiction with the משנה in פאה
steps.stepSummary: רבא raises a contradiction for רב נחמן. He starts by quoting the משנה that lists the מצוות whose 'fruits' a person enjoys in this world while the 'principal' stays for עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised a contradiction for רב נחמן: We learned that there are things a person does and eats their fruits in this world, while the principal stays for him in the next world: honoring parents, acts of kindness, making peace between people, and Torah study equals them all.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. רבא sets up a contradiction, and this is only the first side. He first proves each item on the list (steps 9-11), and the clashing source, the פסוק about שילוח הקן, comes in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says only certain מצוות give reward in this world as well. That suggests other מצוות do not, which the גמרא will set against another source. 'Fruits' means reward now, and 'principal' means the main reward that is kept for later.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction to him

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is only half of רבא's question. The next steps (9-11) prove the list. The clash itself comes in step 12, with the פסוק about שילוח הקן.

phrases.english: Rava raised a contradiction to Rav Nachman:

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאָדָם עוֹשֶׂה אוֹתָן
phrases.english: We learned: These are things that a person does
phrases.notes: משנה פאה 1:1

phrases.english: and eats their fruits in this world
and the principal remains for him for the World-to-Come;
these are: honoring father and mother,
and acts of kindness,
and bringing peace between a person and his fellow;
and Torah study is equal to them all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, moving from stories to a question about reward.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the משנה's list of מצוות that bring reward in this world, which is set against the שילוח הקן פסוק in step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in פאה lists only a few מצוות that give reward in this world, yet שילוח הקן also has a this-world reward פסוק (step 12) and is not listed.

steps.title: Pesukim for honoring parents and doing kindness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק for כיבוד אב ואם and for גמילות חסדים showing that they bring reward in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: For honoring father and mother the Torah says, 'So your days will be long and it will go well with you.' For acts of kindness the פסוק says, 'One who pursues righteousness and kindness will find life, prosperity, and honor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is going through the משנה's list and showing a פסוק for each מצוה that promises reward in this world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Long life, things going well, prosperity and honor are all rewards a person gets in this world. This is the source for the משנה's claim that these מצוות give 'fruits' now. Proving the list item by item also sets up the next question: what about other מצוות with the same kind of promise?

phrases.english: With regard to honoring father and mother, it is written:
"So that your days may be long,
phrases.notes: דברים 5:16

phrases.english: and so that it may go well with you."
With regard to acts of kindness, it is written:
"One who pursues righteousness and kindness
phrases.notes: משלי 21:21

phrases.english: will find life, prosperity, and honor."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוקים behind the משנה quoted in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That כיבוד אב ואם and גמילות חסדים bring reward in this world

steps.title: Making peace is linked to kindness through the word 'pursue'
steps.stepSummary: For הבאת שלום the פסוק says 'seek peace and pursue it,' and רבי אבהו links it by the shared word 'pursue' to the kindness פסוק, so it gets the same reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: For making peace the פסוק says, 'Seek peace and pursue it.' רבי אבהו said: we learn it from the word 'pursue' in both places. Here it says 'pursue it' about peace, and there it says 'one who pursues righteousness and kindness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The peace פסוק does not mention a reward by itself, so רבי אבהו connects it to the kindness פסוק, which does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Seek peace and pursue it' is a command with no promised reward. Since the same word 'pursue' shows up in the kindness פסוק, a גזירה שוה carries over that reward of life, prosperity and honor to making peace.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned (from a word appearing in both places)

steps.confusionAlert: The peace פסוק alone promises nothing. The reward comes only by linking it to the kindness פסוק through the shared word.

phrases.english: And with regard to bringing peace, it is written:
"Seek peace and pursue it."
phrases.notes: תהלים 34:15

phrases.english: And רבי אבהו said:
It is learned from 'pursuing' and 'pursuing.'
phrases.notes: The same word in two פסוקים links them, so what is said in one applies to the other.

phrases.english: It is written here: "Seek peace and pursue it,"
and it is written there: "One who pursues righteousness and kindness."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list and uses the kindness פסוק from step 9 as its base.
steps.raayaObject: That הבאת שלום brings reward in this world
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 34:15 linked to משלי 21:21 by רבי אבהו's word link

steps.title: פסוק for Torah study
steps.stepSummary: For תלמוד תורה the פסוק says 'it is your life and the length of your days.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For Torah study the פסוק says, 'For it is your life and the length of your days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list by showing the reward פסוק for Torah study.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Your life and the length of your days' promises long life, a reward in this world. With this, every מצוה on the משנה's list now has a source.

phrases.english: With regard to Torah study, it is written:
"For it is your life and the length of your days."
phrases.notes: דברים 30:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last item in the list of sources begun in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That תלמוד תורה brings reward in this world

steps.title: Why isn't sending away the mother bird on the list?
steps.stepSummary: שילוח הקן has the same kind of promise ('it will go well with you and you will live long'), so why does the משנה leave it out?
steps.simpleTranslation: For sending away the mother bird, the Torah also says, 'So that it will go well with you and you will have long days.' So let the משנה list this one too!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his challenge to רב נחמן: if a 'this-world reward' פסוק puts a מצוה on the list, שילוח הקן should be there too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method of the last few steps was: find a פסוק that promises reward now, and that proves the מצוה belongs on the list. שילוח הקן has almost the same wording as כיבוד אב ואם, yet the משנה leaves it out. So either the list is incomplete or something else decides what goes on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Sending away the mother bird before taking the eggs or chicks

phrases.english: With regard to sending away the mother bird from the nest, it is also written:
"So that it may go well with you and you will lengthen your days."
phrases.notes: דברים 22:7

phrases.english: So let the משנה also list this one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's contradiction from step 8: by the method of steps 9-11, שילוח הקן should also be on the list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the משנה's list of מצוות that pay 'fruits' in this world
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שילוח הקן has a פסוק promising this-world reward just like כיבוד אב ואם, so by the same reasoning it should be listed.

steps.title: The תנא listed some and left some out
steps.stepSummary: First answer: the תנא simply did not list every case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught some and left some out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a quick answer to רבא: the משנה's list is just examples, not complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תנא ושייר' is a standard answer meaning the list is not meant to be complete. If that is true, leaving out שילוח הקן proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught some and left some out

phrases.english: He taught some and left some out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every מצוה with a this-world reward פסוק must be listed
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא only gave some examples, so שילוח הקן could just be left out

steps.title: But the משנה says 'these are the things'
steps.stepSummary: The answer is pushed away: the משנה opens with 'אלו דברים,' which sounds like a complete, exact list.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא taught 'These are the things,' and you say he taught some and left some out?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רב נחמן's answer from step 13, because the משנה's wording points to a complete list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'These are the things' means exactly these and no others. A list that opens that way cannot be just a sample, so the question about שילוח הקן comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: These are the things (sounds like an exact list)

phrases.english: The תנא taught: "These are the things,"
and you say he taught some and left some out?!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects 'תנא ושייר' for this משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The opening words 'אלו דברים' show the list is complete

steps.title: רבא brings רב אידי's question on a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes what רב אידי taught him about the פסוק 'Say of the צדיק that he is good, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds,' and asks: are there good and not-good צדיקים?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רב אידי explained it to me. The פסוק says, 'Say of the righteous one that he is good, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.' Is there a righteous person who is good and a righteous person who is not good?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a new answer to the שילוח הקן question by quoting a פסוק and pointing out a problem in it. This step sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links 'eating the fruit of their deeds' to a צדיק who is 'good.' That sounds odd, since every צדיק should be good. Answering this question will show which kind of צדיק gets 'fruit' in this world.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there really...? (a question showing something seems strange)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: רַב אִידִי אַסְבְּרַאּ לִי:
phrases.english: רבא said: רב אידי explained it to me:
"Say of the righteous one that he is good,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 3:10

phrases.english: for they shall eat the fruit of their deeds."
Is there a righteous person who is good
and a righteous person who is not good?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא רַב אִידִי אַסְבְּרַאּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 14 rejected 'תנא ושייר,' רבא begins a different answer to the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New idea from a פסוק that explains what decides the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any מצוה with a reward פסוק belongs on the list
steps.terutzMaskana: Being set up: only a certain kind of 'good' earns fruit in this world

steps.title: Good to Heaven and to people
steps.stepSummary: A צדיק who is good to Heaven and to people is a 'good צדיק'; one who is good to Heaven but bad to people is a צדיק who is not good.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: someone who is good to Heaven and good to people is a good צדיק. Someone who is good to Heaven but bad to people is a צדיק who is not good.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers רב אידי's question from step 15 and lays the groundwork for explaining why שילוח הקן is not on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Good' in the פסוק means good toward other people, not only toward Heaven. Since the פסוק gives 'fruit' to the good צדיק, the fruit in this world seems tied to goodness toward people. Honoring parents, kindness and making peace all help other people, which hints at why שילוח הקן is treated differently.
steps.whatToRemember: A 'good צדיק' is good to ה׳ AND to people. The 'fruit' in this world goes with the good done for others.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key to answering why the משנה's list leaves out שילוח הקן even though it has a reward פסוק.

phrases.english: Rather: one who is good toward Heaven and toward people,
that is a good righteous person;
one who is good toward Heaven but bad toward people,
that is a righteous person who is not good.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised on the פסוק in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can there be a צדיק who is 'not good'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Good' means good to people too. A צדיק who is good only to Heaven is a צדיק who is not 'good.'

steps.title: A matching question about the bad רשע
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a parallel פסוק about a 'bad רשע' and asks whether some רשעים are bad and some are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the same way, the פסוק says: 'Woe to the bad רשע, for the deeds of his hands will be done to him.' Is there a רשע who is bad and one who is not bad?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his teaching with a second פסוק that matches the first one. He asks the same kind of question about the רשע, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 the question was about a 'good צדיק.' Here the same strange double wording appears for the רשע: 'רשע רע.' Every רשע sounds bad, so the extra word 'רע' needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: In the same way; along the same lines
What his hands did; the results of his own deeds

phrases.english: In the same way, you say:
"Woe to the wicked one who is bad,
for the deeds of his hands will be done to him."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 3:11, the very next פסוק after 'Say of the צדיק that he is good.'

phrases.english: But is there a wicked one who is bad
and one who is not bad?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to the question in step 15, this time about the רשע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the extra word 'רע' add to 'רשע'?

steps.title: Bad to Heaven and bad to people
steps.stepSummary: A רשע who sins against Heaven and also hurts people is a 'bad רשע'; one who sins only against Heaven is a רשע who is not 'bad.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: one who is bad to Heaven and bad to people is a bad רשע. One who is bad to Heaven but not bad to people is a רשע who is not bad.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his question: the word 'רע' means hurting other people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the same measure: how a person treats others. This finishes the answer to step 12. The fruits of reward in this world come from מצוות that are good to people, and שילוח הקן does not help other people. The גמרא does not say that last point out loud; the learner has to connect it back.

keyTerms.meaning: Bad toward Heaven (sins between a person and ה׳)

steps.whatToRemember: 'Good' and 'bad' in these פסוקים are about how a person treats other people. That is why the משנה lists only מצוות that help others as earning fruits in this world, and leaves out שילוח הקן.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'רשע who is not bad' is still a רשע. He sins against Heaven. The only difference is that he does not hurt other people.

phrases.english: Rather: one who is bad to Heaven and bad to people
he is a bad wicked one;
one who is bad to Heaven but not bad to people
this is a wicked one who is not bad.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 and completes רבא's answer to step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'רע' means harming other people in addition to sinning against Heaven.

steps.title: Merit earns principal and fruits; sin earns only principal
steps.stepSummary: A זכות has a principal and also fruits, while an עבירה has a principal but no fruits. Each part is learned from the two פסוקים in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: A merit has a principal and has fruits, as it says: 'Say of the צדיק that he is good, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.' A sin has a principal and no fruits, as it says: 'Woe to the bad רשע, for the deeds of his hands will be done to him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching. A good deed earns extra reward on top of its basic reward, but a sin gets only its basic punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The picture is borrowed from money: the קרן is the main sum and the פירות are the interest. The צדיק's פסוק mentions eating 'fruit,' so a זכות has extra. The רשע's פסוק mentions only 'the deeds of his hands,' so a sin is punished just for itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Principal; the main sum (the basic reward or punishment)
Fruits; profits or interest (extra reward or punishment)

phrases.english: A merit has a principal
and it has fruits,
as it says: "Say of the righteous one that he is good, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 3:10. The part left out is 'for they will eat the fruit of their deeds,' which is where the fruits come from.

phrases.english: A sin has a principal
but it has no fruits,
as it says: "Woe to the wicked one who is bad, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 3:11. It goes on 'the deeds of his hands will be done to him,' meaning only what he did, with no fruit mentioned.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַזְּכוּת יֵשׁ לָהּ קֶרֶן וְיֵשׁ לָהּ פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same two פסוקים from ישעיהו to teach a new rule about reward and punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זכות earns principal plus fruits; an עבירה earns principal only.

steps.title: A פסוק says sinners eat fruits too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule from a פסוק in משלי that says sinners 'will eat from the fruit of their way.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain the פסוק: 'They will eat from the fruit of their way and be filled with their own plans'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from step 19 with a פסוק that sounds like sins do have fruits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said a sin has no fruits. But this פסוק in משלי is about sinners, and it says they eat 'fruit.' That sounds like extra punishment beyond the principal.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I fulfill (explain) this פסוק?

phrases.english: But then how do I explain:
"They will eat from the fruit of their way
and be filled with their own plans"?
phrases.notes: משלי 1:31. The פסוק is talking about people who did wrong.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that an עבירה has no fruits.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק about sinners says they eat 'fruit,' which means extra punishment.

steps.title: A sin that produces fruits has fruits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a sin which produces further results does have fruits, and a sin which does not produce results has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sin that produces fruits has fruits. A sin that does not produce fruits has no fruits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by splitting sins into two kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'a sin has no fruits' is the normal case. When a sin leads to more results beyond itself, the punishment grows too. That is the case the פסוק in משלי is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: Produces fruits; leads to more results

steps.whatToRemember: A good deed always earns extra. A sin earns extra punishment only when it causes more results beyond itself.

phrases.english: A sin that produces fruits
has fruits.
And one that does not produce fruits
has no fruits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: two kinds of sin
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every sin has no fruits, so the פסוק in משלי seems to contradict the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a sin that produces results has fruits; the פסוק in משלי is talking about that kind.

steps.title: A good thought is joined to action
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ joins a good thought to the deed, learned from the פסוק in מלאכי about 'those who think of His name.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A good thought, ה׳ joins it to the action, as it says: 'Then those who fear ה׳ spoke to each other, and ה׳ listened and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before Him for those who fear ה׳ and for those who think of His name.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching: a good thought gets counted together with deeds. The proof is a פסוק that the next step will explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists two groups in ה׳'s book of remembrance: 'those who fear ה׳' and 'those who think of His name.' The second group is credited just for thinking, which is the basis of this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Joins it; attaches it (ה׳ counts it together with deeds)

phrases.english: A good thought, He joins it to action,
phrases.notes: 'He' means ה׳: He counts the good thought together with real deeds.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אָז נִדְבְּרוּ יִרְאֵי ה׳ אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ
phrases.english: as it says: "Then those who fear ה׳ spoke to one another,
and ה׳ listened and heard,
and a book of remembrance was written before Him
for those who fear ה׳ and for those who think of His name."
phrases.notes: מלאכי 3:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching that continues the theme of reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ joins a good thought to action.

steps.title: What does 'those who think of His name' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words 'and for those who think of His name' mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'and for those who think of His name'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the words in the פסוק. This sets up רב אסי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already mentioned 'those who fear ה׳.' The גמרא wants to know who the extra group of 'thinkers' is.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who think of His name

phrases.english: What is "and for those who think of His name"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the key words of the פסוק in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who are 'those who think of His name'?

steps.title: Planned a מצוה but was prevented: credited as done
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי explains: if a person planned to do a מצוה and was stopped by forces outside his control, the פסוק credits him as if he did it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: Even if a person planned to do a מצוה, and something outside his control stopped him so he did not do it, the פסוק considers it as if he did it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי answers the question and shows how the פסוק proves that a good thought counts like a deed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Those who think of His name' are people who planned a מצוה but could not do it. They are written in the book of remembrance anyway. This only applies when he was stopped by things outside his control (נאנס), not when he simply changed his mind.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains the פסוק
He was stopped by forces outside his control
The פסוק counts it for him

steps.whatToRemember: A real plan to do a מצוה, blocked only by forces outside a person's control, is credited as if the מצוה was done.

phrases.english: רב אסי said:
Even if a person planned to do a מצוה
and he was prevented by forces beyond his control and did not do it,
the פסוק counts it for him as if he did it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: אֲפִילּוּ חָשַׁב אָדָם לַעֲשׂוֹת מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 and grounds the rule of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Those who think of His name' are people who planned a מצוה but were prevented; they are credited as if they did it.

steps.title: ה׳ does not join a bad thought to the deed
steps.stepSummary: A bad thought is not counted by ה׳ as if it were an action, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: ה׳ does not join a bad thought to an action, as it says: 'If I had seen sin in my heart, ה׳ would not hear.'
steps.whatsHappening: Right after saying that ה׳ joins a good thought to the deed, the גמרא teaches the opposite rule for a bad thought: ה׳ does not count it as an action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 22-24 showed that ה׳ credits a good plan as if it were done. Here the גמרא says a bad plan is not punished as if it were done. The פסוק is read as saying that a sin which stayed only in the heart is not held against the person.

keyTerms.meaning: A bad thought or plan to sin
Joins it to the deed, counting the thought as if it were an action

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with Step 22. A good thought is joined to the deed, but a bad thought is not. ה׳ is generous with good plans and lenient with bad ones.

phrases.english: A bad thought,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְצָרְפָהּ לְמַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not join it to an action,
as it says: 'If I had seen sin in my heart,
phrases.notes: תהלים 66:18

phrases.english: ה׳ would not hear.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְשָׁבָה רָעָה אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְצָרְפָהּ לְמַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite rule to Step 22, now for bad thoughts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bad thought alone is not punished as if it were a deed.

steps.title: Challenge from the verse about 'the fruit of their thoughts'
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in ירמיה says ה׳ brings evil as 'the fruit of their thoughts', which sounds like thoughts are punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain the פסוק: 'Behold, I am bringing evil on this nation, the fruit of their thoughts'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule it just gave, using a פסוק that seems to punish people for their thoughts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If bad thoughts are not punished, why does ירמיה say the punishment is the 'fruit of their thoughts'? The words seem to tie the punishment to the thinking itself.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I explain (this פסוק)? A way of asking how a verse fits with the rule

phrases.english: But then how do I explain:
'Behold, I am bringing evil on this nation,
phrases.notes: ירמיה 6:19

phrases.english: the fruit of their thoughts'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule of Step 25 with a contradicting פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that bad thoughts are not joined to the deed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls the punishment the fruit of their thoughts, which suggests thoughts are punished.

steps.title: A thought that bears fruit is joined to the deed
steps.stepSummary: A bad thought that leads to an action is joined to the deed. A thought that leads to nothing is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A thought that produces fruit, ה׳ joins to the action. A thought that has no fruit, ה׳ does not join to the action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק in ירמיה speaks about a thought that actually led to a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is narrowed. When the bad thought produced a deed, the person is punished for the thought too. When the thought stayed only a thought, it is not punished. This matches the pattern of Step 21 about sins that bear fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: That produces fruit, meaning it leads to an action

steps.whatToRemember: A bad thought is punished only when it leads to an actual sin. A bad thought that never turns into action is not punished.

phrases.english: A thought that produces fruit,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, joins it to the action;
a thought that has no fruit,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְצָרְפָהּ לְמַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not join it to the action.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְשָׁבָה שֶׁעוֹשָׂה פְּרִי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְצָרְפָהּ לְמַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of Step 26 by separating two kinds of thoughts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (two types of thought)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to say that every bad thought is punished.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a thought that led to action is joined to the deed.

steps.title: Challenge from 'to catch Israel in their heart'
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in יחזקאל speaks of catching Israel 'in their heart', which sounds like punishment for thoughts alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the פסוק: 'In order to catch the house of Israel in their heart'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק that seems to show people are punished for what is only in their heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer of Step 27 does not fit here. This פסוק seems to describe punishment for the heart itself, even with no action mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: But what about that which is written? An opening for a challenge from a verse
To catch or grab hold of

phrases.english: But what about that which is written:
'In order to catch the house of Israel in their heart'?
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 14:5. The word בית in square brackets is added in the corrected wording of the text.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge from a different פסוק against the rule of Steps 25 and 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a bad thought with no deed is not punished.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק speaks of being caught for what is in the heart alone.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: that verse is about עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in יחזקאל refers to עבודה זרה, which is so severe that even thinking about it is punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: That פסוק is written about idol worship, as the Master said: idol worship is severe, since anyone who denies it is like one who admits to the whole Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers that the פסוק is a special case. It speaks only about עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבודה זרה weighs as much as the whole Torah, since rejecting it counts like accepting all of the Torah. Because it is so serious, it is an exception, and even the thought of it is punished. The general rule for other sins stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: One who denies it, who rejects idol worship

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule about bad thoughts has an exception: for עבודה זרה, the thought alone counts.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
That one is written about idol worship,
as the Master said: Idol worship is severe,
since anyone who denies it
is like one who admits to the entire Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: הָהוּא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 28 by limiting the פסוק to עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the verse to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to be about thoughts of any sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only for עבודה זרה is a thought alone punished, because of how severe it is.

steps.title: עולא explains the verse through רב הונא's teaching
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains the פסוק using רב הונא: once a person sins and repeats it, the sin 'is permitted' to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is like רב הונא, for רב הונא said: once a person committed a sin and repeated it, it is permitted to him.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a different answer to the challenge from יחזקאל, based on a teaching of רב הונא. The very next step will ask what רב הונא's words mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of limiting the פסוק to עבודה זרה, עולא connects it to a person who has sinned again and again. For such a person, the sin has become part of him, so his heart can be held against him.

keyTerms.meaning: Repeated it, did it a second time

phrases.english: Ulla said: It is like Rav Huna,
for Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָבַר אָדָם עֲבֵירָה וְשָׁנָה בָּהּ –
phrases.english: Once a person committed a sin and repeated it,
it is permitted to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 28, in place of רב אחא בר יעקב's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to punish any thought of sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק speaks of someone who repeated his sin until it became habit.

steps.title: Can a sin really become permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the wording of רב הונא: surely a sin does not become allowed just because it was repeated.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It is permitted to him' — can that enter your mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to question רב הונא's words. Taken literally, they cannot be right, and the next step will fix the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sin can never become truly permitted, so 'it is permitted to him' cannot be meant literally. The challenge is aimed at the wording, not at the idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? A way of saying something is impossible

phrases.english: 'It is permitted to him' — can that enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the literal wording of רב הונא in Step 30.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sin cannot actually become allowed by being repeated.

steps.title: It becomes like something permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא means that the sin comes to feel to the person as if it were permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: it becomes to him like something permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording: the sin is not truly allowed, it only feels allowed to the sinner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a person repeats a sin, he gets used to it and stops feeling it is wrong. This is the habit that עולא used to explain the פסוק about being caught in the heart.

keyTerms.meaning: It becomes to him like something permitted

steps.whatToRemember: Repeating a sin makes it feel permitted. It never really becomes permitted.

phrases.english: Rather: it becomes to him like something permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 31 by rereading רב הונא's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הותרה לו seemed to mean the sin is truly allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only feels allowed to the person.

steps.title: Better to sin privately than desecrate ה׳'s name publicly
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו in the name of רבי חנינא teaches that sinning in secret is less bad than חילול השם in public, based on a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי חנינא: It is better for a person to sin in secret and not desecrate the name of Heaven in public, as it says: 'And you, house of Israel, so says ה׳: Each man go serve his idols, and afterward, if you do not listen to Me, but My holy name you shall not desecrate.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אבהו about how serious it is to desecrate ה׳'s name in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to say, 'Go serve your idols if you will, but do not profane My name.' From this, a private sin is treated as less damaging than a public חילול השם. This does not permit private sin. It only shows how severe public desecration is.

keyTerms.meaning: Desecrates the name of Heaven (חילול השם)

steps.confusionAlert: נוח לו does not mean that sinning privately is allowed. It means a private sin is less bad than public חילול השם.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that public חילול השם is treated as worse than the private sin itself.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
It is better for a person
that he commit a sin in secret
and not desecrate the name of Heaven in public,
as it says: 'And you, house of Israel,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 20:39

phrases.english: so says ה׳:
Each man, go serve his idols,
and afterward, if you do not listen to Me,
phrases.notes: The word ואחר in square brackets is added in the corrected wording, matching the פסוק itself.

phrases.english: but My holy name you shall not desecrate.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: נוֹחַ לוֹ לָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching about public חילול השם, after the discussion of thoughts and habitual sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A private sin is less severe than publicly desecrating ה׳'s name.

steps.title: רבי אלעאי's advice to someone overwhelmed by his desire
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי הזקן says that if a person's יצר is overpowering him, he should go where he is unknown, wear black, and act privately, but never cause a public חילול שם שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעאי הזקן said: If a person sees that his evil inclination is overpowering him, he should go to a place where no one knows him, dress in black and wrap himself in black, and do what his heart wants, but he must not desecrate ה׳'s Name in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אלעאי הזקן that continues the theme of רבי אבהו from the previous step: a public חילול השם is worse than a private sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעאי is not praising the sin. He is ranking two bad outcomes: if a sin is going to happen anyway, it should at least not shame ה׳'s Name in front of people. Going far away and dressing plainly keep the act hidden and low.

keyTerms.meaning: The evil inclination, a person's inner pull toward sin
Black clothes, plain and humble garments
Desecrating ה׳'s Name, making Him look bad in people's eyes

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a free pass to sin. In step 36 the גמרא limits this advice to someone who truly cannot control his יצר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ilai the Elder said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם רוֹאֶה אָדָם שֶׁיִּצְרוֹ מִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו –
phrases.english: If a person sees that his inclination is overpowering him,
he should go to a place where they do not know him,
and dress in black, and wrap himself in black,
and do as his heart desires,
but he must not desecrate the Name of Heaven in public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical teaching that supports רבי אבהו's point that a private sin is less bad than a public חילול השם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person overwhelmed by his יצר should act in private and in a humble way rather than cause a public חילול שם שמים.

steps.title: A ברייתא says sinning in secret shows no care for ה׳'s honor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעאי with a ברייתא: one who does not care about his Creator's honor would be better off never born, and רב יוסף says this means someone who sins in secret.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But a ברייתא teaches: Anyone who does not care about his Creator's honor, it would be better for him not to have come into the world. Who is this? רבה says: someone who stares at the rainbow. רב יוסף says: someone who sins in secret!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי אלעאי can advise sinning in private, when a ברייתא, as רב יוסף explains it, treats secret sinning as a terrible thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יוסף, hiding a sin shows that a person fears people more than ה׳. That seems to clash directly with רבי אלעאי's advice to go somewhere unknown and sin quietly.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? Opens a challenge
But was it not taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: Is that so? But was it not taught:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁלֹּא חָס עַל כְּבוֹד קוֹנוֹ –
phrases.english: Anyone who does not care about the honor of his Creator,
it would be fitting for him not to have come into the world.
What is this?
phrases.notes: Meaning: who counts as someone who does not care about ה׳'s honor?

phrases.english: Rabba says: This is one who gazes at the rainbow.
phrases.notes: The rainbow is compared to the look of ה׳'s glory, יחזקאל 1:28.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף אוֹמֵר: זֶה הָעוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה בַּסֵּתֶר!
phrases.english: Rav Yosef says: This is one who commits a sin in secret!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אלעאי's advice from step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעאי's advice to sin privately in a place where one is unknown
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יוסף reads the ברייתא as condemning secret sinning as a lack of care for ה׳'s honor, which contradicts recommending it.

steps.title: Two different people: one who can control himself and one who cannot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא speaks of someone who can control his יצר, while רבי אלעאי speaks of someone who cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one speaks about someone who is able to bend his inclination, and that one speaks about someone who is not able to bend his inclination.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each source is talking about a different kind of person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person could hold back and still sins in secret, he shows he only fears people, so the ברייתא condemns him. רבי אלעאי's advice is only for someone truly overpowered; for him, at least keeping it private avoids a public חילול השם.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the sources do not truly clash

steps.whatToRemember: Secret sinning is condemned for someone who could control himself. רבי אלעאי's advice is only for someone truly unable to, so that he at least avoids a public חילול השם.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one is where he is able to bend his inclination,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that condemns secret sinning.

phrases.english: and that one is where he is not able to bend his inclination.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעאי's advice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 35.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source speaks about a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעאי and the ברייתא seemed to give opposite judgments on secret sinning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of one who can control his יצר; רבי אלעאי speaks of one who cannot.

steps.title: The משנה: no credit for חילול השם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: אין מקיפין בחילול השם, whether the person sinned by accident or on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: There is no credit given for desecrating ה׳'s Name, whether it was done by accident or on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה about how severe חילול השם is, which sets up a question about what its unusual phrase means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of how serious חילול השם is. The משנה says this rule applies even when it was done by accident, but its key phrase, אין מקיפין, is unclear, and the next steps explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Credit is not given; nothing is put off for later

phrases.english: We learned there in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: See אבות 4:4, which also says accidental and deliberate חילול השם are treated the same.

phrases.english: Credit is not given for desecrating the Name,
whether by accident or on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from secret versus public sin to another source about the severity of חילול השם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For חילול השם, credit is not given, whether it was done by accident or on purpose.

steps.title: What does אין מקיפין mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the phrase אין מקיפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "credit is not given" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the משנה's wording and sets up two explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מקיפין comes from giving something on credit, but it is not clear how that applies to חילול השם. The next two steps give two different answers.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "credit is not given"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the משנה from step 37.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of אין מקיפין in the context of חילול השם

steps.title: מר זוטרא‎: ה׳ is not like a storekeeper who gives credit
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא explains that ה׳ does not act like a storekeeper who lets you pay later; the punishment for חילול השם is not delayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: It means that one does not act like a storekeeper.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives the first explanation of אין מקיפין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A storekeeper lets customers take now and pay later. For most sins ה׳ may wait, but for חילול השם the bill is not put off.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
That one does not act like a storekeeper.
phrases.notes: A storekeeper lets you pay later; here the punishment is not put off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אין מקיפין means the punishment for חילול השם is not delayed, unlike a storekeeper's credit.

steps.title: מר בריה דרבנא: חילול השם tips a balanced scale
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבנא explains that if a person's merits and sins are equal, the sin of חילול השם tips the balance toward guilt.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבנא said: It comes to say that if the scale was evenly balanced, it tips it.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בריה דרבנא gives a second, different explanation of אין מקיפין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the phrase as being about weighing merits against sins. When the two sides are equal, חילול השם alone is heavy enough to tip the scale toward the side of sins.

keyTerms.meaning: מר, son of רבנא, an אמורא

steps.whatToRemember: Two readings of אין מקיפין: מר זוטרא says the punishment for חילול השם is not delayed; מר בריה דרבנא says it tips an evenly balanced scale toward guilt.

phrases.english: Mar son of Rabbana said:
It comes to say that if it was evenly balanced, it tips the scale.
phrases.notes: The balance between his merits and sins; the חילול השם tips it toward the sins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation that differs from מר זוטרא's in step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אין מקיפין means that when merits and sins are equal, חילול השם tips the scale toward guilt.

steps.title: A new ברייתא begins with the word 'Always'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a ברייתא with 'תנו רבנן' and its first word, 'לעולם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught in a ברייתא: Always...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by starting to quote a ברייתא. Only the opening words appear here, and the actual teaching comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תנו רבנן' tells us that a ברייתא is being quoted, not a statement from an אמורא. 'לעולם' means 'always', so the teaching that follows is meant to be a constant way a person should behave. It comes right after the talk of merits and sins being equal in Step 40.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our Rabbis taught': the standard way the גמרא opens a quote from a ברייתא.
Always: introduces a rule meant to apply at all times.
A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a complete teaching by itself. 'Always' is just the opening word, and you need the next words to know what a person should always do.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: Always

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After מר בריה דרבנא's point in Step 40 that one sin can tip an even balance, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that opens with 'Always'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the opening words of a ברייתא appear here ('Always...'). Its full ruling comes in the next lines.
